bubble_sort.title: Bubble Sort
bubble_sort.description: Repeatedly steps through the list, compares adjacent elements, and swaps them if they are in the wrong order.
bubble_sort.pseudocode:
BUBBLE-SORT-ASCENDING(A)
    FOR i ← 0 TO length(A) - 1
        swapped ← FALSE
        FOR j ← 0 TO length(A) - 2 - i
            IF A[j] > A[j + 1]
                SWAP A[j] AND A[j + 1]
                swapped ← TRUE
            END IF
        END FOR
        IF swapped = FALSE
            BREAK
        END IF
    END FOR
    RETURN A

selection_sort.title: Selection Sort
selection_sort.description: Repeatedly finds the minimum element from the unsorted part and puts it at the beginning.
selection_sort.pseudocode:
SELECTION-SORT(A)
    FOR i ← 0 TO length(A) - 1
        minIndex ← i
        FOR j ← i + 1 TO length(A) - 1
            IF A[j] < A[minIndex]
                minIndex ← j
            END IF
        END FOR
        SWAP A[i] AND A[minIndex]
    END FOR
    RETURN A

insertion_sort.title: Insertion Sort
insertion_sort.description: Builds the sorted array one item at a time by inserting elements into correct order.
insertion_sort.python:
def insertion_sort(arr):
    """Sort an array using Insertion Sort."""
    a = arr.copy()
    for i in range(1, len(a)):
        key = a[i]
        j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 and a[j] > key:
            a[j + 1] = a[j]
            j -= 1
        a[j + 1] = key
    return a
insertion_sort.pseudocode:
INSERTION-SORT(A)
    FOR i ← 1 TO length(A) - 1
        key ← A[i]
        j ← i - 1
        WHILE j >= 0 AND A[j] > key
            A[j + 1] ← A[j]
            j ← j - 1
        END WHILE
        A[j + 1] ← key
    END FOR
    RETURN A

merge_sort.title: Merge Sort
merge_sort.description: Divide and conquer algorithm that recursively splits arrays and merges sorted halves.
merge_sort.pseudocode:
MERGE-SORT(A)
    IF length(A) <= 1 RETURN A
    mid ← floor(length(A) / 2)
    left ← MERGE-SORT(first half of A)
    right ← MERGE-SORT(second half of A)
    RETURN MERGE(left, right)

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
problems.description: Combine two pre-sorted arrays into a single sorted array.
problems.pseudocode:
MERGE-TWO-SORTED-ARRAYS(A, B)
    result ← empty array
    i ← 0, j ← 0
    WHILE i < length(A) AND j < length(B)
        IF A[i] <= B[j]
            APPEND A[i] TO result; i ← i + 1
        ELSE
            APPEND B[j] TO result; j ← j + 1
        END IF
    END WHILE
    APPEND remaining elements TO result
    RETURN result

quick_sort.title: Quick Sort
quick_sort.description: Partitions array around a pivot so smaller elements go left and larger elements go right.
quick_sort.pseudocode:
QUICK-SORT(A, low, high)
    IF low < high
        pivotIndex ← PARTITION(A, low, high)
        QUICK-SORT(A, low, pivotIndex - 1)
        QUICK-SORT(A, pivotIndex + 1, high)
    END IF

binary_search.title: Binary Search
binary_search.description: Searches a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.
binary_search.pseudocode:
BINARY-SEARCH(A, T)
    low ← 0, high ← length(A) - 1
    WHILE low <= high
        mid ← floor((low + high) / 2)
        IF A[mid] = T RETURN mid
        ELSE IF A[mid] < T low ← mid + 1
        ELSE high ← mid - 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN -1

problems.title: First Occurrence
problems.description: Find first occurrence index of duplicate target in sorted array.
problems.pseudocode:
FIRST-OCCURRENCE(A, T)
    low ← 0, high ← length(A) - 1, answer ← -1
    WHILE low <= high
        mid ← floor((low + high) / 2)
        IF A[mid] = T
            answer ← mid, high ← mid - 1
        ELSE IF A[mid] < T low ← mid + 1
        ELSE high ← mid - 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN answer

graph_bfs.title: Breadth-First Search (BFS)
graph_bfs.description: Explores graph level by level starting from a source node using a Queue data structure.
graph_bfs.pseudocode:
BFS(G, S)
    visited ← {S}, queue ← [S], order ← []
    WHILE queue is not empty
        u ← DEQUEUE queue, APPEND u TO order
        FOR each neighbor v of u in ascending order
            IF v is not in visited
                ADD v TO visited, ENQUEUE v
            END IF
        END FOR
    END WHILE
    RETURN order

problems.title: Shortest Path in an Unweighted Graph
problems.description: Find shortest edge count distance from source to destination.
problems.pseudocode:
SHORTEST-PATH-BFS(edges, S, D)
    IF S = D THEN RETURN 0
    visited ← {S}, queue ← [(S, 0)]
    WHILE queue is not empty
        (u, distance) ← DEQUEUE queue
        FOR each neighbor v of u
            IF v = D THEN RETURN distance + 1
            IF v is not in visited
                ADD v TO visited, ENQUEUE (v, distance + 1)
            END IF
        END FOR
    END WHILE
    RETURN -1

graph_dfs.title: Depth-First Search (DFS)
graph_dfs.description: Explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking.
graph_dfs.pseudocode:
DFS(G, S)
    visited ← empty set, order ← empty list
    DFS-VISIT(S)
    RETURN order

DFS-VISIT(u)
    ADD u TO visited, APPEND u TO order
    FOR each neighbor v of u in ascending order
        IF v is not in visited THEN DFS-VISIT(v)
    END FOR

problems.title: Detect a Cycle
problems.description: Detect if back-edges exist forming a cycle in the graph.
problems.pseudocode:
HAS-CYCLE(G)
    visited ← empty set
    FOR each vertex u in G
        IF u is not in visited AND DFS-CYCLE(u, parent = NONE) = TRUE
            RETURN TRUE
    END FOR
    RETURN FALSE

bst.title: Binary Search Tree (BST)
bst.description: Inserts and searches nodes in a binary tree where left child < root < right child.
bst.pseudocode:
BST-INSERT(root, value)
    IF root = NULL RETURN NEW NODE(value)
    IF value < root.value root.left ← BST-INSERT(root.left, value)
    ELSE IF value > root.value root.right ← BST-INSERT(root.right, value)
    RETURN root
